Cranberry Fig Jam for Cheese Boards, Sandwiches and Gifting

By Chris Scheuer | Updated on November 9, 2026
This Cranberry Fig Jam combines tart cranberries, sweet dried figs and bright mandarin oranges with ginger, warm spices and a splash of balsamic vinegar. It’s delicious on cheese boards, buttery biscuits and turkey sandwiches, and makes a lovely homemade gift.

What if you could solve your holiday appetizer dilemma AND check a whole bunch of gifts off your list in one fell swoop, with less than 30 minutes of hands-on time? This easy Cranberry Fig Jam is your ticket! Make a batch for your holiday cheese boards, then tuck a few jars away for neighbors, coworkers, teachers, and friends with our free printable labels!

Made with dried figs and fresh or frozen cranberries, this sweet-tart jam comes together in under an hour, with the stovetop doing most of the work. There's no need to wait for fresh fig season, either. Keep a bag of cranberries in the freezer, and you can stir up a batch any time of year!

This Cranberry Fig Jam is a fun, festive addition to our collection of easy fig jams, all made with dried figs! If you've ever eyed those little jars in a fancy gourmet shop, you know they can come with a hefty price tag. Making your own costs a fraction of the price, and you'll have plenty to enjoy and share!

A delicious combination of simple ingredients

The ingredient list for this Cranberry Fig Jam is a little unexpected, and that's part of the fun! Dried Mission figs bring rich sweetness, fresh or frozen cranberries add a lively tartness, and mandarin juice and zest brighten everything up.

Brown sugar and honey round out the sweet-tart flavor, while fresh ginger, cinnamon, and a small touch of curry powder add warmth. A splash of balsamic vinegar ties it all together. The result? A jam that's equally at home on your morning toast and your fanciest-danciest holiday cheese board!

How it works

This Cranberry Fig Jam comes together in a few simple stages, with most of the cooking time free for you to do something else nearby.

Start by zesting and juicing the mandarins, then snip the stems from the dried figs and cut them into quarters. Combine the figs and mandarin juice with the brown sugar, water, honey, balsamic vinegar, ginger, and spices.

Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to maintain a steady simmer, then cover and cook for 20 minutes to soften the figs.

Next, take the pot off the heat and use an immersion blender to break down the softened figs. Leave a little texture, but blend away any large pieces.

I like to tip the pot to one side while blending to keep the jam from splashing.

Stir in the cranberries.

Return the mixture to a boil and cook, covered, for another 10 minutes.

Give the jam one more blend, making it as smooth or textured as you like.

Let a spoonful cool completely before checking the consistency. It will thicken as it cools and continue to firm up in the jars, so aim for a slightly looser consistency than you think you want.

Once you're happy with the texture, stir in the reserved mandarin zest for a bright finishing touch. Spoon into clean jars, refrigerate promptly and start dreaming about your first cheese board!

So many delicious ways to enjoy it

Once you have a jar of this Cranberry Fig Jam tucked in the fridge, you'll find all kinds of reasons to pull it out!

  • For an easy appetizer: Add a small bowl to a cheese or charcuterie board with crackers, sliced baguette, and your favorite cheeses. It's wonderful with creamy Brie, tangy goat cheese, or sharp cheddar.
  • For breakfast: Spread it on buttery toast, English muffins, or warm biscuits. A spoonful also adds a delicious sweet-tart touch to oatmeal or yogurt.
  • For an unforgettable turkey sandwich: Spread it on good bread, then pile on sliced turkey and your favorite cheese. It's reason enough to look forward to Thanksgiving leftovers!
  • For waffles and pancakes: Spoon a little over the top along with a pat of butter for a fun change from maple syrup.

And don't save it just for company or the holidays. A little cheese, a few crackers, and a spoonful of jam make an ordinary afternoon feel like a small celebration!

A little gift from your kitchen

There's something special about receiving a gift that someone made just for you, especially when it's something delicious! A jar of this Cranberry Fig Jam makes a thoughtful treat for neighbors, coworkers, teachers, hostesses, and friends.

Add one of our pretty printable labels and a ribbon, and your gift is ready to go. For something a little extra, pair a jar with a wedge of cheese and a package of good crackers. Just remember, this jam needs to stay refrigerated or frozen. Keep your gift jars chilled until you deliver them, and let recipients know how to store their delicious treat.

Whether you're getting a head start on holiday gifts, putting together a cheese board or simply giving your morning toast a delicious little upgrade, this Cranberry Fig Jam is a lovely little thing to have tucked away. Make a batch, save a jar for yourself and spread a little cheer with the rest!

Café Tips for making this Cranberry Fig Jam
  • Start with dried figs. I use dried Mission figs for this recipe. Be sure to snip off the tough stems before cutting the figs into quarters. Kitchen shears make this quick and easy!
  • Sticky figs? If the figs stick to your shears, lightly coat the blades with a little neutral oil or cooking spray.
  • Fresh or frozen cranberries work well. Keeping a bag in the freezer means you can make this jam even after cranberry season has come and gone.
  • Zest before you juice! It's much easier to zest whole mandarins than squeezed halves. Remove just the colorful outer peel, avoiding the bitter white pith. Save the zest to stir in at the very end.
  • Don't worry about an exact cup of juice. Mandarins vary in size and juiciness. A little more or less than 1 cup is fine.
  • Not a curry fan? No worries! I still recommend including the small amount of curry powder. It adds a gentle warmth that blends beautifully with the other ingredients, without a noticeable curry flavor.
  • Use a roomy pot with a tight-fitting lid. You'll need space for the cranberries and room to blend without splashing. Keep the pot tightly covered during the first cooking stage so you don't lose too much liquid.
  • An immersion blender makes things easy. You can blend the jam right in the pot! Remove the pot from the heat first and keep the blender head submerged. I like to use a pot holder to carefully tilt the pot slightly to one side, giving the blender a deeper pool to work in.
  • Keep your blender handy. You'll use it once to break down the softened figs and again after cooking the cranberries. Leave a little texture or blend until smooth, whichever you prefer.
  • Check the consistency with a cooled spoonful. Hot jam looks thinner than the finished spread. Let a spoonful cool completely before deciding whether it needs adjusting. It will continue to thicken in the jars, so aim for a slightly looser consistency than you think you want.
  • Too thick or too thin? Both are easy fixes! If the jam is too thick, stir in water, 1-2 tablespoons at a time. If it's too thin after cooling, simmer uncovered for another 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently, then check another cooled spoonful.
  • Plan ahead for gifting. Wash your jars and lids before you start, and have them ready for the finished jam. Refrigerate (or freeze) promptly after portioning, keep gift jars chilled until delivery.

Cranberry Fig Jam

Chris Scheuer
This Cranberry Fig Jam combines tart cranberries, sweet dried figs and bright mandarin oranges with ginger, warm spices and a splash of balsamic vinegar. It's delicious on cheese boards, buttery biscuits and turkey sandwiches, and makes a lovely homemade gift.
Prep Time 20 minutes mins
Cook Time 30 minutes mins
Total Time 50 minutes mins
Servings 124 servings
Calories 26
PRINT PIN COMMENTS
Prevent your screen from going dark

Ingredients
 
 

  • 6 medium mandarin oranges or 8 small mandarins, for zest and approximately 1 cup juice (Clementines, Halos, or tangerines will also work.)
  • 10 ounces dried Mission figs, I like Mission figs, but other figs will also work. Turkish figs will give a lighter colored finished product.)
  • 2⅓ cups brown sugar, packed - I like dark brown sugar for a deep, mahogany-hued jam, but light brown sugar also works!
  • 3 cups water
  • ⅓ cup honey
  • ¼ cup balsamic vinegar
  • 1½ tablespoons finely grated fresh ginger, or ginger paste
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • ½ teaspoon curry powder
  • 24 ounces fresh cranberries, two 12-ounce bags

Instructions
 

  1. Wash and dry the mandarins. Using a fine zester, zest 3 medium mandarins or 4 small mandarins, avoiding the white pith. Set the zest aside.
  2. Cut all the mandarins in half and juice them. You should have approximately 1 cup of juice; a little more or less is fine. Set aside.
  3. Using kitchen shears, snip off and discard the tough fig stems. Cut the figs into quarters.
  4. Rinse the cranberries in a colander, discarding any soft, shriveled or damaged berries. Drain well.
  5. For the jam:
  6. Combine the mandarin juice, figs, brown sugar, water, honey, balsamic vinegar, ginger, cinnamon and curry powder in a large pot with a tight-fitting lid. Stir well and bring to a boil over medium heat.
  7. Reduce the heat slightly, maintaining a steady boil. Cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through and replacing the lid after stirring.
  8. Remove the pot from the heat. Carefully blend with an immersion blender until no large pieces of fig remain, leaving a little texture. Keep the blender head submerged to prevent hot splashes. I like to use a pot holder to carefully tilt the pot slightly to one side, making it easier to blend. Keep your immersion blender handy; you'll use it again.
  9. Stir in the cranberries. Return to a boil, then cover and cook for 10 minutes, adjusting the heat as needed to prevent the mixture from boiling over.
  10. Remove the pot from the heat and carefully blend again, leaving some texture or blending until smooth, as desired. The jam will thicken as it cools.
  11. Let a spoonful of jam cool completely before checking the consistency. You're looking for a loose, spreadable consistency. If it seems too thick, stir water into the pot, 1-2 tablespoons at a time, until you reach your desired consistency. The jam will continue to thicken as it sits in the jars, so aim for a slightly looser consistency than you think you want.
  12. If the cooled spoonful seems too thin, simmer the jam uncovered for another 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently, then check another cooled spoonful.
  13. Stir in the reserved mandarin zest. Divide the jam into clean, heat-safe containers for cooling and refrigerate promptly.

Notes

The recipe makes 8 cups of jam. The number of jars will depend on the size of your jars.
